question: Why do pregnant women often develop mild anaemia during pregnancy?

options.B: Plasma volume increases more than red blood cell mass
options.C: Suppression of bone marrow by hormones
options.D: Rapid destruction of red blood cells by the placenta

explanation: Haemodilution occurs because plasma volume increases much faster than the number of red blood cells, lowering haemoglobin concentration. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T1#GNS121_U7_T1_h1)

question: When does blood volume reach its highest level during a normal pregnancy?

options.C: At the end of the first trimester

explanation: Maternal blood volume rises progressively through the first and second trimesters, reaching its maximum volume near the middle of the third trimester. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T1#GNS121_U7_T1_h1)

question: How much total iron does a woman need throughout a normal pregnancy?
explanation: The body needs roughly one thousand milligrams of extra iron to support the baby, placenta, and larger blood volume. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T1#GNS121_U7_T1_h2)

question: A pregnant woman at thirty weeks has low serum ferritin despite normal eating habits. What does this usually mean?

options.A: Destruction of red blood cells due to blood group incompatibility
options.B: Her gut cannot absorb any supplements
options.C: Normal use of stored iron for maternal and fetal needs
options.D: An infection causing iron storage in the liver

explanation: Falling ferritin levels during pregnancy generally reflect the normal depletion of maternal iron stores as the body uses them up. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T1#GNS121_U7_T1_h2)

question: Which white blood cell type mostly causes the higher total white blood cell count in pregnancy?
explanation: An increase in circulating neutrophils accounts for most of the rise in total white blood cell count seen in healthy pregnant women. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T1#GNS121_U7_T1_h3)

question: Why is it tricky to interpret a high white blood cell count in a pregnant woman?

options.B: White blood cell counts drop very low in the final trimester
options.C: Lab reagents do not work well with pregnant blood
options.D: Pregnancy naturally raises white blood cell counts without an infection

explanation: Because healthy pregnant women often have elevated white blood cell counts, nurses cannot rely on this lab value alone to diagnose infection. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T1#GNS121_U7_T1_h3)

question: Why does the body naturally increase blood clotting tendencies during pregnancy?

options.A: To clear waste products faster from the baby
options.B: To prevent heavy bleeding during delivery and after the placenta separates
options.C: To speed up red blood cell production
options.D: To help move iron across the placenta

explanation: Increased clotting factors prepare the maternal body to quickly stop bleeding when the placenta detaches from the uterine wall. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T1#GNS121_U7_T1_h4)

question: Which clotting factor increases a lot during pregnancy, raising the risk of blood clots?
explanation: Fibrinogen levels rise substantially during gestation, promoting clot formation and increasing the likelihood of thrombosis. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T1#GNS121_U7_T1_h4)

question: What is the normal expected blood loss during a standard vaginal delivery?
explanation: Normal blood loss during a standard vaginal delivery is generally estimated to be around five hundred millilitres or less. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T1#GNS121_U7_T1_h5)

question: Why might a haemoglobin test right after birth show a deceptively high result?

options.A: Fetal blood mixes with maternal blood
options.B: Dehydration from labour thickens the blood sample
options.C: Rapid red blood cell production during second-stage labour
options.D: A sudden drop in plasma volume concentrates the blood temporarily

explanation: When the extra fluid volume suddenly drops after delivery, the blood momentarily becomes more concentrated before tissue fluids shift back. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T1#GNS121_U7_T1_h5)

question: How does a woman's body mainly get rid of extra fluid weight right after delivery?
explanation: Women quickly get rid of the extra fluid weight after birth through profuse urination and sweating. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T1#GNS121_U7_T1_h6)

question: A woman who had a caesarean section is resting in bed on her first day. Why is she at high risk for a blood clot?

options.A: Sudden loss of white blood cells after surgery
options.B: High clotting factors combined with staying in bed
options.C: Rapid return of normal plasma volume

explanation: Because clotting factors stay high for weeks after birth, immobility after surgery greatly increases the danger of blood clots forming in the legs. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T1#GNS121_U7_T1_h6)

question: What is a key nursing priority for pregnant women attending an antenatal clinic in Nigeria?

options.B: Advising total bed rest for nine months
options.C: Encouraging iron and folic acid supplements alongside good local foods
options.D: Telling patients to drink less water

explanation: Ensuring mothers take their iron and eat nourishing local foods helps prevent nutritional anaemia during pregnancy. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T1#GNS121_U7_T1_h7)

question: Why do nurses encourage women to walk around soon after delivery?

options.A: It forces the kidneys to work faster
options.B: It stops the uterus from contracting
options.C: It stimulates red blood cell production
options.D: It helps prevent blood clots by keeping leg blood moving

explanation: Getting women to walk around soon after birth keeps blood moving in their legs, lowering the risk of dangerous blood clots. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T1#GNS121_U7_T1_h7)
